idiom_name: sealed interface nodes + data class copy() + List<Frame> path
implementation_notes: Sealed hierarchies plus an exhaustive `when` give the total navigation the pattern wants, and a data class copy() rebuilds the parent in one line, so the whole realization is a sealed interface Tree, a data class Branch(kids: List<Tree>) and a Loc holding the focus plus a List<Frame> where a frame is the parent branch and the child index. What replaces the classic structure is copy() plus sealed exhaustiveness; what is still hand-written is the context type, and the standard library offers no persistent collections, so structural sharing for long child lists comes from kotlinx.collections.immutable (PersistentList) or from keeping lists small. The mutable alternative - a parent-pointer class graph - remains the right choice for UI models edited in place.
pitfalls: data class equals/hashCode are deep and recursive, so comparing locations or storing them in a Set walks the subtrees and can StackOverflowError on deep trees.
copy() is a shallow copy: a MutableList child leaks mutation into the previous version, so children must be List (or PersistentList) and never cast back to MutableList.
Sealed hierarchies are closed per module and package - that is what makes `when` exhaustive, so adding a node kind breaks every navigation site at compile time by design.
Recursive descent over a deep tree can overflow the stack; navigate with the explicit path list rather than recursive calls.
